en: One fascicle of the Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī.
Compiled by the Grand Master of State Ceremonial, Extraordinary Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su.

The Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—honored with a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and bestowed the posthumous name Dajian (Great Mirror)—translated this by imperial decree. Now, as for the method of reciting dhāraṇīs:
First, within the Samaya Maṇḍala,
one beholds the assembly of noble beings, receives empowerment, and recognizes the tutelary deity;
from the master, one receives the samaya.
Then, in a secluded place within the mountains or in a pure chamber,
one should paint an image of the Honored One, the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī,
and install it on the eastern wall.
The practitioner facing it should dig a pit in the ground one and a half cubits deep at the place of recitation. If there are any tiles,
rubble, bone ashes, hair, or other impure substances within the earth, [they must be removed].
One must remove them in both cases.
If there are none, one should take earth from its original site to fill the area,
piling it up until it is level and even.
If there is excess soil, that ground is auspicious.
Mix cow dung with earth and plaster the ground to make it level and even.
Furthermore, take cow dung mixed with water;
recite the Aparājita Dhāraṇī twenty-one times to consecrate the cow dung.
The mantra for the Invincible One (*Ajita*) is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām*, oṃ, hulu hulu, caṇḍāli, mātaṅgi, svāhā. Having performed the consecration (*adhiṣṭhāna*) with this, [one should proceed].
Thereafter, begin from the northeast corner and apply it while circling to the right.
Next, take the leaves of a hibiscus or lotus seeds and rub them [upon it] until it becomes bright and clean.
Above that, take white powder and mix it with water;
use a cord to divide it into nine positions and mark them.
Grind white sandalwood on a stone and apply it to the nine positions.
Regarding these nine positions:
the position of Vairocana Buddha is established in the center;
the position of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is established on the right side.
Behind Avalokiteśvara,
establish the position of Maitreya Bodhisattva;
behind the position of Vairocana Buddha, [establish the position of Mañjuśrī].
Establish the position of Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
To the left of this bodhisattva,
establish the position of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
To the left of the position of Vairocana Buddha,
establish the position of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
Below the position of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva...
Establish the position of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Before Vairocana Buddha,
establish the position of Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin Bodhisattva.
To the right of the position of Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
place the position of Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha;
these are called the nine positions.
Anoint it with white sandalwood incense to serve as the seat for inviting the worthy sages and saints.
Place a canopy over the ears and suspend banners on all four sides.
At the four sides of the site of enlightenment,
one should offer milk gruel in the early morning;
at the time of the midday meal, one should offer curd-rice along with sweet and rich foods.
There were various syrups along with assorted fruits.
Four incense burners were placed at the four gates,
and four pure water jars were placed at the four corners.
Place fragrant water in a vessel and insert flowers or branches from a tree with green leaves as an offering.
At the four corners, light four butter lamps.
In front of the maṇḍala, before the seat of the practitioner performing the recitation,
place two bowls of *argha* perfumed water as an offering.
One may take gold, silver, refined copper, porcelain, or new earthenware vessels; alternatively, one may use a conch-shell cup or fresh, clean leaves.
All others are unsuitable.
When wishing to place food within them, one must first wash the vessel thoroughly.
Cover it with fragrant smoke to fumigate the interior.
Once the food has been placed inside, it must again be fumigated with fragrant smoke.
Then, sprinkle water empowered by the Aparājita Dhāraṇī upon it.
Then, arrange the items in a clockwise direction within the mandala.
Afterward, place a low-legged stool before the mandala,
with its legs half an inch above the ground.
Either a mat of *kuśa* grass or a pure substance shall be used as a seat for the practitioner to sit upon.
The practitioner should perform a thorough ritual bath before reciting.
The method for bathing is as explained in the Susiddhi;
alternatively, one may bathe by means of the Dharma,
taking the contemplation of the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā) as the bath.
Alternatively, whether as a layperson or a monastic, one may take the upholding of the fundamental disciplinary precepts (*śīla*) without any transgression as one's ritual bathing.

Or, three times each day before the Buddha, one may prostrate to the Buddha, confess and repent, rejoice in merit, entreat [the Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma], make vows, and dedicate the merit.
One should use it for bathing;
or, by empowering it seven times with a pure mantra,
one should use it for purification.
While bathing and reciting correctly, one should contemplate that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, and thus one also attains purity.
Forming this mental attention, one then recites the mantra for bathing:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ. Recite this daily upon entering the maṇḍala.
One should determine the appropriate times:
either two times, namely early morning and dusk;
or three times, adding noon.
Alternatively, one may perform the practice four times a day by adding midnight to the [usual] sessions.
Or, according to the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
one should do so every fifteenth day of the waxing moon.
It eliminates karmic obstacles, increases merit, and prolongs life.
By vowing to recite this one thousand times,
one realizes supramundane samādhi and attains the dhāraṇī of non-forgetfulness.
On that day, it is best not to eat for one full day and night;
alternatively, one may consume the "three white foods," namely milk,
curd, and non-glutinous rice.
Either gruel constitutes the middle grade,
or a regular vegetarian meal constitutes the lower grade;
one should wear clean clothing.
The mind should be reverent and pure in faith,
free from hesitation.
If one wishes to perform the recitation:
Upon arriving at the site of practice, first place both knees upon the ground.
Pay homage to Vairocana Buddha and the eight great bodhisattvas;
confess and repent openly, and make the five great vows.
First, I vow to deliver boundless sentient beings.
Second, I vow to accumulate boundless merit and wisdom.
Third, I vow to study boundless Dharma gates.
Fourth, the matter of the Tathāgatas' boundless vows;
fifth, the vow to accomplish unsurpassed bodhi.
Sitting in the full lotus posture, anointing the hands with incense, one binds the samaya-mudrā and recites the mantra as follows:
Namo samanta buddhānām | Asme trisme samaye svāhā | [Recite this while forming] its mudrā.
Joining the two palms with the two thumbs extended constitutes the mudrā;
it is applied to five locations:
the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat.
Each person recites the mantra once, consecrating it and scattering it upon their crowns.
By the majestic spiritual power of the samaya mudrā and mantra,
one is able to purify the stages of the Tathāgata’s grounds and bring the pāramitās to perfection.
One is able to accomplish both mundane and supramundane siddhis.
Next, bind the Dharmadhātusaṃbhava mudrā and recite the mantra:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ dharma-dhātu-svabhāvātmako hūṃ*. As for the manner of binding the mudrā: [perform the gesture].
Place both thumbs within the palms and form fists.
Extend both index fingers, keeping them side by side and joined together.
Place it upon the crown of the head;
from the crown, let it gradually descend and disperse downward.
Recite the mantra three times.
One should then contemplate one’s own body as being identical to the *dharmadhātu*,
free from all material forms and characteristics, like empty space.
Next, one binds the *vajrasattva-dharmacakra-mudrā* and recites the mantra, saying:
Namo samantavajrāṇām | Oṃ vajratma jñāṃ | [Form the mudrā.]
Interlace the backs of the two hands,
place the left thumb within the palm of the right hand so that it touches the right thumb, and then recite the mantra three times.
One attains the state of oneself as Vajrasattva.
Next, the mantra for binding the Vajra Armor mudrā is:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām oṃ vajrakavaca hūṃ*. As for the form of this mudrā:
With both hands, join the palms hollowly.
Place each index finger on the back of its respective middle finger.
Join the two thumbs together.
Form the mudrā upon the middle joint of the middle finger.
As with the previous five locations, recite the mantra once at each.
Through this empowerment, one’s own body becomes clad in the adamantine armor (*vajrakavaca*).
No celestial Māras whatsoever can approach him.
Next, the mudrā and mantra of Acala are as follows:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa krodha hūṃ trāṭ haṃ khaṃ*. To bind the mudrā, each of the two hands uses its thumb.
Press the tips of the little fingers and ring fingers together.
Extend the middle fingers and join the index fingers side by side.
The left hand forms the sheath and the right hand forms the blade.
Forming the right-hand sword-seal by inserting the blade into the sheath and rotating it to the left, one expels all obstructing māras within the maṇḍala;
by rotating it to the right, one binds the boundaries of the eight directions, as well as the zenith, nadir, and intermediate points.
Then, one should visualize Mount Sumeru within the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Upon the summit of the mountain, one should visualize a pavilion made of the seven precious substances.
Within that pavilion...
Vairocana Buddha is surrounded by a retinue of eighty koṭis of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who have perfected the ten stages (bhūmi),
with four Bodhisattvas at each of the four gates and four corners, as well as the eight offering goddesses.
With inner and outer offerings,
visualize their presentation with complete clarity.
Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the assembly of noble Tathāgatas and recite the mantra:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | oṃ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānakūśalamūlaparigraha svāhā*. To form the seal, interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward and raise them.
Extend the index finger of the right hand and bend it into the shape of a hook.
Recite [the mantra] three times; by the majestic power of this mudrā and mantra, [the desired result is achieved].
The Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and the assembly of noble ones,
not failing their original vows, have all gathered together.
Next, form the seal for offering the seat and recite the mantra as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām*. (Recite "Aḥ" with an acute accent. For the mudrā of the seal: join the two hands in the hollow-heart *añjali*;
join the two little fingers and the two thumbs together.
The remaining six fingers are slightly extended and bent like a blooming lotus.
Recite [the mantra] three times.
By the power of this mudrā and the mantra, [the desired result is achieved].
From it flow forth all manner of exquisite jewel thrones,
like clouds over the ocean,
offered to the Tathāgata and the entire assembly of noble ones.
Next, offer the arghya water while reciting the mantra:
*Namo samantabuddhānām, āgana samasama svāhā*. Then, with both hands, hold the vessel at the level of the forehead.
Kneeling with lowered body, recite this three times.
Offer *argha* water for the bathing of the holy assembly.
Next, form the mudrā for offering scented ointment and recite the mantra as follows:
*Namo maṇḍalabuddhānām* (1) *viśuddhakṣāntinirvāṇāya svāhā* (2). As for the mudrā: extend the right hand with the palm facing outward.
Grasp the right wrist with the left hand and recite [the mantra] three times. By the power of this mudrā and mantra,
oceans of clouds of all kinds of unguents will flow forth.
Make offerings to all Tathāgatas and the assembly of noble ones.
Next, form the mudrā for presenting flower garlands and recite the mantra:
*Namo samantabuddhānām, mahā-maitry-abhiyunakti svāhā*. As for the ritual gesture (*mudrā*): with both hands...
Crossing the hands with palms facing upward and touching the tips of the index fingers together, recite [the mantra] three times.
By the power of this mudrā and the mantra:
Cloud-seas of all kinds of flower garlands flow forth,
making offerings to the assembly of all Tathāgatas and holy ones.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for offering incense are as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām | Dharma-dhātvanugate svāhā. As for the mudrā: with both hands, palms facing upward.
With the little, middle, and ring fingers bent upward and their backs joined together,
recite [the mantra] three times.
By the power of this mudrā and mantra, [the desired result is attained].
From it flow forth oceans of clouds of all kinds of incense,
making offerings to all Tathāgatas and the assembly of noble ones.
Next, bind the mudrā for presenting food and drink and recite the mantra, saying:
*Namo samantabuddhānām*. *Ara ara kara mara mara mṛtyuñjaya mahāmṛtyu svāhā*. As for the mudrā: with palms hollowed and closely joined, open them like a vessel.
Recite this three times.
Through the power of this seal and mantra,
boundless clouds and oceans of food and drink will flow forth.
Make offerings to all the Tathāgatas and the assembly of noble ones.
Next, form the mudrā for presenting the lamp-light and recite the mantra:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ tathāgatājñā-spharaṇa-vyāpasaṃna-gaganodariye svāhā*. As for the ritual gesture (*mudrā*): form a fist with the right hand and extend the middle finger.
Press the middle joint of the middle finger with the thumb and recite [the mantra] three times.
By the power of this mudrā and mantra, [the desired result is attained].
It emits clouds and oceans of all kinds of radiant lamps as offerings to all Tathāgatas and the assembly of noble ones.
Furthermore, as it is taught in the Mahāyāna sūtras of the Tathāgata:

One should visualize clouds of offerings—such as banners, canopies, pennants, nets, necklaces, garments, and silken streamers—pervading the entire realm of phenomena like a vast ocean; then, with words of truth, one praises them with these verses:
By the power of my merit, the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
and the power of the Dharma-realm, may I abide in universal offering.
Next, perform the mudrā and recite the mantra of the consort Ākāśagarbha:
*Namo samantabuddhānām. Svāhā kham unagate sphara hiṃ gagana svāhā.* As for the mudrā: interlace the two hands in the añjali gesture, with the right hand pressing down upon the left.
Recite this seven times.
Next, visualize within your own heart a perfectly clear and distinct full moon disc.
Visualize the syllable *khaṃ* upon the lunar disc;
it is white in color and emits great radiance.
Illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions,
one contemplates the meaning of the true reality (*dharmatā*) of the syllable *si*:
namely, that all phenomena are equal to empty space.
Free from all forms and characteristics and free from all obstructions,
one then contemplates oneself within the reality of the ultimate truth as the form of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāramitā Buddha-Mother.
The left hand holds a lotus flower,
upon which is a five-pronged vajra;
the right hand forms the upturned palm gesture.
With his hand hanging down, he forms the mudrā of granting boons;
adorned with a crown and necklaces,
his countenance is compassionate, manifesting the power to deliver all sentient beings.
Having performed this visualization,
cross the two hands externally to form fists,
and extend the two middle fingers upright.
With this Vajrapāramitā mudrā,
empower the four places— namely, sealing the heart,
forehead, throat, and crown of the head.
Having performed the mudrā, one should release it and recite the Vajrapāramitā mantra:
Oṃ sattvavajri hūṃ. While performing the mudrā at the four locations, [one should recite this].
Recite each one once.
Then, place the aforementioned mudrā upon the forehead and recite three times;
this constitutes the consecration (*abhiṣeka*). Having completed the consecration:
With the hands positioned on both sides of the seal,
place the vajra-fists behind the crown of the head.
Recite the mantra as follows:
Recite "Oṃ vajrapiñcha" three times,
and then immediately form the Armor Seal (*kavaca-mudrā*):
with both hands, each form a vajra-fist.
Each raises the index finger to the heart,
entwining them like a succession of armor;
one does likewise behind the back.
Next, [the hands] move from the navel to the two knees,
then circle behind the waist and gradually reach the heart.
Next, they proceed to the two shoulders in the same manner.
Next, following the crown of the head down to the nape of the neck and forward to the forehead,
one should again place both vajra-fists behind the brain,
then gradually lower the hands to both sides until they rest slowly.
In the manner of hanging a sash,
one should clap the palms of both hands three times and recite the Armor-Mantra as follows:
Oṃ chindhi chindhi. The mantra for clapping the hands is:
Oṃ vajra tuṣye huḥ. Having visualized oneself as having become the principal deity, [one recites this].
Join the two palms together and bend the two thumbs so that their nail beds face away from each other.
Press the tips of the two index fingers with the two thumbs,
as if making the gesture of snapping the fingers.
Then he recited the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī, saying:
*Namaḥ bhagavate tathāgatāya pratyavekṣaṇajñānavaśavartine buddhāya...*

13. *Ābhiṣeṇa* (repeated as above). 14. *Sugata-varavajraṇa*. 15. *Mṛtyu-niṣūdana*.
16. *Jahāra āhāra*. 17. *Āyur-vināśana*. 18. *Śū*.

Nineteenth, the sound of recitation is neither too high nor too low, neither too slow nor too hurried;
with single-minded focus, one takes Vairocana Buddha as the object of contemplation.
With complete clarity, recite [the mantra] seven times; having done so, seal it upon the crown of the head and disperse the mudrā.
Then, take the bodhi-seed rosary and place it within the palms of the hands.
Recite the mantra for empowering the rosary:
Oṃ virujanmara svāhā. Having recited it seven times, place it upon the crown of the head with the left hand.
Be careful.
Hold the beads.
Move the beads with the right hand.
Each time one utters "Svāhā" in unison with the rosary, move one bead.
Continue reciting until one hundred and eight repetitions,
or even up to one thousand.
He then took the pearl and placed it within his palms;
joining his hands, he rested them upon the crown of his head and made pure and sublime aspirations for what he sought.
May all sentient beings fully attain this.
Then, bind the mudrā of the Honored One and recite [the mantra] seven times or three times.
Again, bind the Vajra-pāramitā mudrā.
Furthermore, bind the five kinds of offering mudrās and perform the offerings while reciting the five kinds of mantras.
Perform as described above.
Then, bind the seal of Acala and recite [the mantra] once;
by turning the seal counter-clockwise, the boundary is dissolved.
Holding an argha vessel, present it as an offering; then,
immediately forming the aforementioned samaya-mudrā,
offer it above the crown of the head.
Recite the Samaya-mantra once.
Without releasing this mudrā, recite the Vajra-vimukti-mantra, saying:
Oṃ vajramukha muḥ. This concludes the dismissal of the assembly of Buddhas and noble ones.
Having performed the preceding acts of prostration, disclosure and confession, sympathetic joy, entreaty, aspiration,
and dedication, one exits the maṇḍala and subsequently remains in a quiet place.
Recite and study Mahāyāna sūtras;
contemplate the ultimate truth (paramārthasatya);
and dedicate this sublime merit toward that which is sought.
It assists in accomplishing siddhi.
If performing the rite for pacification (śāntika),
one faces north and the mandala is circular.
Visualize the assembly of noble ones as white in color;
all the articles of offering within the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) are white.
They are dressed in white robes and sit facing north.
When burning aloeswood incense for the rite of increase (*puṣṭi*),
one should sit facing east;
the deity, the offerings, and the clothing of oneself must all be yellow.
When burning white-altar incense for a rite of subjugation (*abhicāra*),
one should sit facing south;
the deity, the offerings, and the clothing should all be blue or black in color.
Burn frankincense.
If performing a rite of attraction (vaśīkaraṇa),
sit facing west.
Visualize the deity as red in color;
likewise, all food, drink, and clothing are red.
Burn ghee and blended incense.
